tasks.description: In .github/workflows/ci.yml's jest job, replace the single `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` step with: a step reading the installed Playwright version into a step output; an actions/cache@v4 step for ~/.cache/ms-playwright keyed on runner.os, the image (ubuntu-24.04) and that version; a browser step running `npx playwright install chromium` with one retry, timeout-minutes 3, continue-on-error true and a ::warning:: on failure; a font step running `timeout 90 npx playwright install-deps chromium` with timeout-minutes 2, continue-on-error true and a ::warning:: on failure. Update the comment above the steps to say why. Serves O1, O2, O3. Dependencies: none.

requirements.statement: An apt-mirror outage can never stop "Run Jest" from running: the Chromium install in the "Jest (hooks)" job is bounded in time, does not depend on apt for the browser itself, and a failed install lets "Run Jest" run anyway. Must pass.

When Chromium cannot be installed, every non-browser Jest suite still runs and reports, and only the three suites that drive Chromium (design-render.test.js, design-render-walk.test.js, design-bundle.test.js) fail, with a message naming the missing browser; the job ends red, never green (D13 unchanged). Must pass.
On a healthy runner the job still installs Chromium, runs every suite including the three render suites, and finishes well inside its 10-minute limit. Not marked must-pass.

requirements.source: TRD Master Task List, FIX-001 acceptance criteria (a)

requirements.statement: No step in the jest job contains `--with-deps`, and every step before "Run Jest" that can touch the network has its own timeout-minutes and continue-on-error: true (checked by reading the YAML with a parser, not grep).
requirements.source: TRD Master Task List, FIX-001 acceptance criteria (b)

requirements.statement: With PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH pointed at an empty temp dir, `npx jest --runInBand --config jest.config.ci.js` fails ONLY suites among the three Chromium suites, each failure naming "Chromium is not installed", and every other suite passes (local stand-in for check 3).
requirements.source: TRD Master Task List, FIX-001 acceptance criteria (c)

requirements.statement: With the browser present, the same jest command passes all suites (local stand-in for check 2).
requirements.source: TRD Master Task List, FIX-001 acceptance criteria (d)

requirements.statement: Decision rule: continue-on-error hides a failed install on the step's own tick, so a failed install must surface elsewhere: the three Chromium suites fail with "Playwright's Chromium is not installed" (design-render.js:755), and each install step emits a ::warning:: annotation on failure.
requirements.source: TRD Decision section, paragraph after the three steps

requirements.statement: Outage time budget: 2 + 3 + about 1.5 (Jest) + about 0.5 (setup), roughly 7 minutes, inside the unchanged 10-minute job limit.
Non-goal: no change to design-render.js, the render tests, or D13's fail-not-skip behaviour.
Non-goal: no change to the job-level timeout-minutes 10, the runs-on ubuntu-24.04 pin, or the "Run Jest" command and its comments.
Non-goal: no change to any other CI job.

could_not_verify: The apt outage, the cache hit, and the job's wall-clock behaviour exist only on the GitHub Actions runner (verification.md §5). They are proven by the fix's PR run (check 2) and the temporary /etc/hosts outage simulation (check 3), both at ship time, not by /implement-trd's local verification.

Whether any render test depends on the nine font packages: inferred not (the byte checks compare renders within one run), and moot while the bounded font step remains; a PR run with fonts absent (check 3) settles it.
open_questions: OQ-1: Should a run that cannot install Chromium end green or red? Assumed: red, non-browser suites run and report, the three Chromium suites fail (owner's call, default taken in the bug report). Owner-only.
